Subject: Redwood Dedicated — initial provisioning requests

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward with Redwood Dedicated for our customer-facing inference tier (Launchpad). Core asks up front: a multipool design (web-serving pool + batch pool), autoscale that supports sustained bursts during marketing spikes, and a regional failover strategy for the US and EU.

Attached is a rough sizing workbook from our infra team — helps show expected qps and token distribution. Key constraints from procurement: 12-month commitment window preferred, but we need predictable top-line monthly spend and an SLA for <120ms p95 on the web-serving pool.

Can you outline what provisioning looks like (lead times, pool sizes, burst policies) and any procurement steps for Marketplace or direct contract?

Thanks,
Alex Torres
VP Product, Lumina Commerce
[Attachment: lumina_sizing_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: ava_chen@redwood.ai
To: Alex Torres <alex@luminacorp.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated — initial provisioning requests

Alex — great to hear. High level response below; I'll loop in Ben for commercial + Marissa for the CS/implementation plan.

1) Timeline & lead times: baseline provisioning for first pool (web-serving) is 10 business days once PO/commit is in. Batch pool provisioning is concurrent; actual multi-pool cutover to production typically 3–4 weeks for staging, perf testing, and canary routing.

2) Pool sizing recommendation: start with a 6-GPU web pool (A100-class equiv) plus a 4-GPU batch pool; we can scale to N+ based on observed token throughput. We will provide quantization recommendations and a kernel profile to optimize p95.

3) Autoscale & burst: we offer burst capacity in two modes — "reserved burst" (pre-allocated burst slots within your commit) and "elastic burst" (pay-as-you-go overage). Suggested autoscale policy: baseline target CPU/GPU utilization 60% with aggressive horizontal spin-up above 75% and a 90s cooldown for web-serving to keep p95 stable.

4) Region selection & failover: primary in us-west1, secondary in eu-west1. We recommend active-standby for web-serving with traffic steering at the edge (DNS failover) and active-active for batch where eventual consistency is acceptable.

5) Procurement options: we can do direct invoiced contract or Marketplace listing (faster for procurement teams). Ben will share checklist for both.

I've attached an ops note with the phases and checkpoints (Marissa will run the activation sprints). Proposed next step: 30-minute kickoff this Wed to review sizing and sign-off on commit type.

Best,
Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Putting commercial notes here for the kickoff: 

- Pricing: recommend a 12-month reserved commitment with monthly billing. We can include 20% of requested burst capacity in the commit as reserved burst to lower unit cost; the remainder can be elastic burst billed on usage.
- SLA addendum: Lumina requires p95 <120ms on web-serving. We can add a service addendum with the usual credits for missed p95 windows; engineering will need to agree to trajectory for kernel tuning and prefilling KV caches as part of the activation.
- Marketplace vs Direct: marketplace shortens procurement by removing PO hoops but has a revenue share. For large enterprise procurement teams, direct invoiced contract is common.

I'll prepare a short commercial checklist for the kickoff (SOW template, PO items, billing contacts). Planning to propose a call Wed 10:00 PT.

—Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Alex / team — I'm Marissa on CS; I'll own the activation sprints and the multiphase rollout. Quick run-down of our recommended activation milestones: 

Phase 0 — Provisioning & Access (day 0–10): network peering, IAM roles, KMS integration for keys, initial pools up in staging.
Phase 1 — Perf & Safety validation (week 2): load tests, latency profiling, KV cache warmups, safety/eval checks on prod-like traffic.
Phase 2 — Canary traffic & ops playbooks (week 3): route 5–10% traffic to new pool, validate autoscale behavior under synthetic spikes.
Phase 3 — Go-live & monitoring ramp (week 4): full cutover, daily SRE runbooks for 2 weeks, QoS checks.

For autoscale thresholds: we'll start with Ava's baseline (60/75/90s cooldown) and iterate during load tests. I will also deliver a runbook for incident responses tied to autoscale events (who to page, rollback criteria).

Please confirm the procurement path (Marketplace vs direct) during the Wed call so we can schedule provisioning windows.

Thanks — looking forward.
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
